title: Moderate prenatal alcohol exposure differentially alters acute ethanol sensitivity of GABAergic transmission in CRFR1- and CRFR1+ CeM Neurons.
ehr_evidence: Whole-cell electrophysiology was performed in the CeM to assess the actions of acute EtOH (44, 66, & 88 mM) on GABAergic transmission onto CRFR1+ and CRFR1- neurons in adult CRF1-Cre-tdTomato rats.
summary: This animal study exposed pregnant CRF1-Cre-tdTomato rat dams to vaporized ethanol on gestational day 12 and used whole-cell electrophysiology to assess sex- and cell type-specific effects of moderate PAE on acute ethanol modulation of GABAergic transmission onto CeM CRFR1+ and CRFR1- neurons in adult offspring.
key_findings: PAE increased basal sIPSC amplitude of CRFR1+ neurons in both sexes (F(1,127) = 5.026, p = 0.027), indicating postsynaptic modifications.
In air males, 66 mM EtOH significantly decreased sIPSC frequency (t(11) = 2.658, p = 0.022), whereas PAE males were insensitive to acute EtOH at all concentrations.
PAE males showed a significant decrease in sIPSC frequency at 44 mM in CRFR1+ neurons (t(8) = 2.465, p = 0.039) with a main effect of exposure (F(1,59) = 7.255, p = 0.009).
PAE females showed significant decreases in CRFR1- sIPSC frequency at 44 mM (t(11) = 3.805, p = 0.003) and 66 mM (t(9) = 2.775, p = 0.022) with a main effect of exposure (F(1,57) = 4.070, p = 0.048).
PAE females showed significant decreases in CRFR1+ sIPSC frequency at 44 mM (t(8) = 3.196, p = 0.013) and amplitude at 44 mM (t(9) = 2.719, p = 0.023).
Air-exposed control females were unresponsive to acute EtOH in both cell types across all concentrations.
study_design: Animal experimental study (prenatal alcohol exposure model with whole-cell electrophysiology)
population: Adult CRF1-Cre-tdTomato rats (P80-105), both sexes, bred in-house at Binghamton University
exposure_domain: Prenatal alcohol exposure (moderate, gestational day 12 vaporized ethanol, target BEC 60-120 mg/dL)
limitations: Use of transgenic CRF1-Cre-tdTomato reporter line may alter neurophysiology via insertional mutagenesis, promoter promiscuity/leakiness, and transient reporter expression not reflecting endogenous receptor timing.
Recordings performed at room temperature rather than physiologically relevant temperature.
Findings limited to adult rats and cannot be generalized to humans.
Single gestational exposure window (G12) limits understanding of dose-response and timing effects.
